notes: Loop 3 re-check (loop 2: 8.4). I checked the phone screenshots first (landing, /r#demo, /r#demo-ai, /r#demo-result, /r#demo-price, all 11 /try screens, try-report, try-rehearsal), then desktop and dark. All five loop-2 items are fixed or nearly: six distinct interview answers (report.txt:480-512); a /try rehearsal button that draws the grid at 390 px (try-rehearsal-phone.png); one German word, Gewinnschwelle, explained as 'auf Englisch: Break-even' (report.txt:257-259); and the after-test chart with '(gemessen)', a Demo-Daten chip and its own screenshot. The landing page now honestly calls step 4 'zwei Zahlen'. New: the AI demo is a fourth tab on every report and opens with 'Von einer KI: die ausgedachten Gäste gespielt'. Dark mode is calm, and the German number formats hold. Held back: on /r#demo-ai, step 5 looks exactly like the rule-based one. There is no 'von Claude gespielt' badge before the caveat, and every AI-written sentence is behind a tap (report-ai-phone.png slices 5-6). The after-test number line crowds four labels, and the 7 tick runs through 'Holt den Test herein: 11'. Step 4's caption describes two lines that stay hidden until the reveal. On a 1280 px laptop, the header button wraps to a second row. No cap applies.
improvements: /r#demo-ai step 5 (src/report/rehearsal.ts; report-ai-phone.png slices 4-6): make the AI-played run look different from the rule-based one. Today the header chips, the dots, the grid and the folds are the same as on /r#demo, and 'jeweils eine KI (Claude)' appears only in the caveat at the bottom (report-ai.txt:396). Add a 'Von Claude (KI) gespielt' chip next to 'Ausgedacht' in the step-5 header and in the grid caption. Open the interview by default on this demo, and draw two answers as quote cards with a small Claude tag (Paweł's 7,90 €, Greta's Mensa). Add a link in the ribbon that jumps to step 5. Why: rehearsal visuals and the use-of-AI criterion. A judge scrolling on a phone sees no AI in the step where it worked. Done when the first screen of step 5 in report-ai-phone.png shows the chip and at least one AI-written quote.

After-test number line (/r#demo-result, src/report/charts.ts; report-result-phone.png at about y 11,400-11,540): four labels sit in about 60 px. The 'Trägt sich: 7' tick runs through the 'H' of 'Holt den Test herein: 11', and 'Erwartet: 8' loses its leader line. On phones, put the two thresholds (7 and 11) below the axis and the three guesses above it, or list them under the line. Why: this chart is the payoff of the learning loop and should read at a glance. Done when no tick crosses a label at 390 px in all four languages (the Spanish and Polish labels are longer).

Step 4 caption (report.txt:273; src/report/sections.ts, step 4): 'Die durchgezogene Linie markiert … die gestrichelte …' describes two marker lines that stay hidden until the owner guesses (report-phone.png slice 4 and report-slider-moved.png show neither). Show this sentence only after 'Meine Schätzung prüfen' or 'Einfach zeigen', or write 'Nach Ihrer Schätzung erscheinen zwei Linien: …'. Add one note on rounding: the line crosses 0 € at about 10,2, and the marker sits at 11 because guests come whole. Why: the slider must explain a mechanism, not point at marks that are not drawn. Done when the caption before the reveal names only what is on screen.

Landing page (site/index.html:202; landing-phone.png slice 6; landing-desktop.png top): the Claude-played demo is the strongest proof of what the AI does, but its only landing link sits about 8,000 px down on a phone, inside 'Ehrlich gebaut'. Add it to the 'Die KI redet' card ('Sehen Sie, wie Claude 6 Gäste spielt →') or as a third link in the hero. Also fix the 1280 px header, where 'Mit Ihren Zahlen testen' wraps to a second row under the logo: shorten it to 'Testen' or drop one nav item. Why: the landing page should teach the method in under a minute, so the first laptop screen should be one tidy row and show where the AI acts. Done when the first two phone screens of the landing page link to /r#demo-ai and the desktop header is one row.

Rule-based interview (src/sim interview lines; report.txt:480-512): the answers are now distinct, but all six share one frame ('Ich habe … / … erzählt / Wenn …, bleibe ich dabei'). Leyla wants the bowl 'so voll … wie am ersten Tag' although she never ate it. Vary the sentence shape by persona and only refer to what the persona did in her own rounds. Why: next to the Claude run's natural answers, the rule-based ones read as a template, which is honest but flat. Done when no two answers share their last clause and every reference matches that persona's grid.
pitchIn60s: It looks and reads like a lesson, not a dashboard. It opens with who did what, asks you to guess the break-even before the reveal, and then a slider moves the chart, the euro readout and a 'Warum sich das geändert hat' sentence that adds up to the cent. The worst case is drawn against your spare cash, a living Kiez grid follows the imagined customers, the test card prints on one page, and an after-test chart puts reality on the same line as your guesses. It works in four languages with correct number formats, on a phone and in dark mode. /try asks one question per screen and now ends with a rehearsal. The new Claude-played demo is one tap away on every report, but it looks like the rule-based one until you open the folds.
standout: Step 4's guess-first slider. 'Bevor Sie hinsehen: Schätzen Sie selbst' hides the answer. Then one drag moves the line, the marker, the euro readout and a sentence you can check by hand: 8 × 5,35 € − 36,57 € = 6,23 €, and 6,23 € × 10 − 180 € = −117,70 € (report.txt:306).
weakest: /r#demo-ai step 5 looks the same as the rule-based grid. The AI-written words and the 'played by Claude' label are behind taps or at the bottom of the step.
